verbs.name: snapshot
verbs.help: reads the screen: every element with its id, role, name, state and bounds

fields.name: text
fields.help: the screen as one text: one line per element, nested by indent; a line's state words, each written only where the element states it, are enabled or disabled, checked or unchecked, value=, selected or unselected, pressed or unpressed, invalid and focused; a mixed toggle reads unpressed, and a grammar or spelling error reads invalid

verbs.name: click
verbs.help: clicks the element an id names, then settles

args.name: id
args.help: the id of the element to click, as a snapshot lists it

fields.name: settled
fields.help: whether the app went quiet after the step

fields.name: busy
fields.help: the class of work still outstanding, present only when `settled` is false; the step ran and is not rolled back

fields.name: added
fields.help: the elements on the screen after the step that were not on it before

fields.name: removed
fields.help: the ids of the elements that were on the screen before the step and are not on it after

fields.name: changed
fields.help: the elements on the screen before and after the step whose role, name, state, bounds or parent differ, as they read after it; `selected` and `pressed` are left out where the element states neither, `pressed` is false for a mixed toggle, and `invalid` is true for a grammar or spelling error

verbs.name: type
verbs.help: types text into the element an id names, replacing what the element holds, then settles; an empty text clears it

args.name: id
args.help: the id of the element to type into, as a snapshot lists it

verbs.name: press
verbs.help: presses one key on the focused element, then settles

args.name: key
args.bound: one name of the key list
args.help: the key to press: one name of the key list

args.name: shift
args.help: whether shift is held while the key is pressed; false when absent

verbs.name: advance
verbs.help: moves the app's time forward by `ms` milliseconds, then settles; an app moves time in its own units, and `advanced_ms` is the time it actually moved, never more than asked

args.name: ms
args.help: how far to move the app's time, in milliseconds

fields.name: advanced_ms

verbs.name: scroll
verbs.help: brings the element an id names into view, then settles

args.name: id
args.help: the id of the element to bring into view, as a snapshot lists it

fields.name: settled
fields.help: whether the app went quiet after the step

fields.name: busy
fields.help: the class of work still outstanding, present only when `settled` is false; the step ran and is not rolled back

fields.name: added
fields.help: the elements on the screen after the step that were not on it before

fields.name: removed

fields.name: in_view
fields.help: whether the element is in view after the step; false when scrolling could not bring it there, and an action on it would still be refused `off-screen`

verbs.name: screenshot
verbs.help: the screen, or the element an id names, as a PNG image; an element shot is cropped to the part of its bounds that can be seen; in a build that paints overlay scrollbars, a scrollbar thumb painted within 0.7 s of a scroll fades by wall time

args.name: id
args.help: the id of the element to crop to, as a snapshot lists it; the whole screen is taken without it

fields.name: width
fields.help: the image's width, in pixels

fields.name: height
fields.help: the image's height, in pixels

fields.name: png
fields.help: the image: a PNG of 8-bit RGBA pixels as painted, written as base64 text

verbs.name: start
verbs.help: starts a session on the app a name names and answers once it is up

args.name: app
args.help: the app to hold: one name of the apps the binary boots

fields.name: label
fields.help: the name of the app the session holds

fields.name: pid
fields.help: the process id of the session's host

fields.name: idle_expiry_s
fields.help: the seconds without a request after which the host stops the session by itself; each answered request starts the count again

verbs.name: status
verbs.help: reaches the session and says what holds it

fields.name: label
fields.help: the name of the app the session holds

fields.name: pid
fields.help: the process id of the session's host

fields.name: served
fields.help: how many requests the host had answered before this one

fields.name: idle_expiry_s
fields.help: the seconds without a request after which the host stops the session by itself; each answered request starts the count again

verbs.name: stop
verbs.help: stops the session and returns once nothing of it is left

fields.name: stopped
fields.help: true once the session is gone

verbs.name: help
verbs.help: describes the tool itself, as one document: every verb with its arguments and its result fields, the keys of a node, the key names, the busy classes, the refusal causes with their remedies, the command line's exit statuses and the session errors with their remedies

fields.name: verbs
fields.help: every verb, in the table's order, keyed name, level, help, args and fields; each argument keyed name, kind, bound, required and help, each result field keyed name, kind, always and help

fields.name: node_keys
fields.help: the keys of a node in a nodes field, in the order a node is written with them, keyed name and help

fields.name: key_names
fields.help: the names a key argument admits

fields.name: busy_classes
fields.help: the classes of work a busy field names

fields.name: causes
fields.help: every cause a refusal names, keyed name, meaning and remedy

fields.name: exit_statuses
fields.help: the statuses a run of the command line ends with, keyed status, name and meaning

fields.name: session_errors
fields.help: every error a session edge ends a command with, keyed kind, meaning and remedy

node_keys.name: id
node_keys.help: the element's stable id, the one a call names it by

node_keys.name: parent
node_keys.help: the id of the element's parent; left out for a root

node_keys.name: role
node_keys.help: the element's role, as the accessibility tree reads it

node_keys.name: name
node_keys.help: the element's accessible name, as the accessibility tree reads it; empty where it has none

node_keys.name: enabled
node_keys.help: for an element that can be disabled, whether it lacks a `disabled` attribute: the reading follows the attribute's presence, whatever its value; left out for every other element

node_keys.name: checked
node_keys.help: for a checkbox or a radio input, whether it is checked; left out for every other element

node_keys.name: value
node_keys.help: for a text-entry input or a textarea, the text it holds, else its `value` attribute; a password or a file input that holds a value reads a fixed mask; left out for every other element

node_keys.name: selected
node_keys.help: whether the element states itself selected by `aria-selected`; left out where it states neither

node_keys.name: pressed
node_keys.help: whether the element states itself pressed by `aria-pressed`; left out where it states neither; a mixed toggle reads false

node_keys.name: invalid
node_keys.help: whether the element states itself invalid by `aria-invalid`; a grammar or spelling error reads true

node_keys.name: focused
node_keys.help: whether the element holds the document's focus

node_keys.name: bounds
node_keys.help: where the element stands on the screen: x, y, width and height, in pixels; a box reads the same bounds however far its content is scrolled

node_keys.name: differs
node_keys.help: on a changed node only: the keys whose reading differs from before the step, in this order; a node that only moved reads bounds alone

causes.name: unknown-verb
causes.meaning: the call names no verb of the verb set
causes.remedy: use a verb the verb list names

causes.name: malformed
causes.meaning: the call's arguments are not the ones the verb's schema states
causes.remedy: pass exactly the arguments the verb's schema names, each of the kind and within the bound it states

causes.name: not-found
causes.meaning: no element on the screen reads the id
causes.remedy: take a snapshot and use an id it lists

causes.name: stale
causes.meaning: the id read an element earlier in this session and no element reads it now
causes.remedy: the screen changed since the id was read: take a new snapshot and act on what it lists

causes.name: disabled
causes.meaning: the element carries the `disabled` attribute, which the snapshot reads as not enabled
causes.remedy: the control is disabled: change the state that disables it, then act again

causes.name: covered
causes.meaning: another element is hit at the point the action would land; a hit reaches content clipped by `contain: paint`, so an element lying where such content extends can read `covered` though nothing shows over it; a box clipped on one axis stops a hit at its whole padding box, so an element lying outside it along the axis it does not clip can read `covered` though it shows
causes.remedy: another element covers this one: act on the covering element or dismiss it first

causes.name: off-screen
causes.meaning: the element lies outside the viewport, or outside the visible part of a scrolling box that holds it
causes.remedy: the element is out of view: bring it into view with `scroll`, then act again

causes.name: time-unavailable
causes.meaning: the app this session holds gives it no way to move its time
causes.remedy: this session cannot move time: act without `advance`, or start a session whose host supplies a time step

causes.name: fonts-unavailable
causes.meaning: the app this session holds has no font it can paint text with
causes.remedy: boot the app with a font it can decode

exit_statuses.name: accepted
exit_statuses.meaning: the command ran: its answer on stdout as one line of JSON; a step that ran and did not go quiet is accepted, and its `settled` reads false

exit_statuses.name: refused
exit_statuses.meaning: the command was refused and ran nothing: the refusal on stdout as one line of JSON, naming its cause and its remedy; a word that is no verb and an argument the verb's schema does not admit are refusals

exit_statuses.name: usage
exit_statuses.meaning: the line is no command: one fixed line on stderr and nothing on stdout; no command, an argument that is not text, a `--session` that is absent where the verb needs one or is given twice, an app the binary does not boot

exit_statuses.name: session-error
exit_statuses.meaning: a session edge stopped the command: the error on stdout as one line of JSON, naming its kind and its remedy, and its fixed message on stderr

session_errors.remedy: stop the running session, or name another state directory
start a session in this state directory, or name the directory a running session uses
start a session in this state directory, or name the directory a running session uses

session_errors.meaning: the session host exited before it answered
session_errors.remedy: start the session again, and if its host exits again, name another state directory

session_errors.meaning: the session did not answer in time
session_errors.remedy: the command may have run: ask `status`, then take a snapshot before acting again

session_errors.meaning: the session answered outside its protocol
session_errors.remedy: stop the session with the binary that started it, or name another state directory

session_errors.meaning: a session label is 1 to 32 bytes of a-z, 0-9 and -
session_errors.remedy: name an app of 1 to 32 bytes of a-z, 0-9 and -, as the apps list names it

session_errors.meaning: the session state directory's path is too long for a socket: as given, it is at most 94 bytes
session_errors.remedy: name a shorter path for the state directory, or a relative one, which counts only its own bytes

session_errors.meaning: the session state directory is open to its group or to others
session_errors.remedy: name a new state directory, or make this one open to its owner only

session_errors.meaning: the session lifecycle is not supported on this platform
session_errors.remedy: hold the session in process instead: the `mcp` role holds it in its own process

session_errors.meaning: a session input or output step failed
session_errors.remedy: check that the state directory exists and its owner can write it, then retry

session_errors.meaning: the instance did not go quiet after a step
session_errors.remedy: the call ran and is not rolled back: take a snapshot to read the screen as it stands

session_errors.meaning: the answer is larger than the session carries; the call ran and is not rolled back
session_errors.remedy: the call ran and is not rolled back: take a snapshot to read the screen as it stands
